thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: gpu-capacity-exhaustion - high queue depth and failed scale operations in us-east-1. Affected pool: gpu-infer-main. Auto-scale requests returned 429 and 500s. Notifying oncall.

jenn (oncall): on it. Initial readouts: request queue jumped from 4k -> 27k in ~9m. p99 latency up from 150ms -> 3.7s. Error spike on gen endpoints (502/504s). Any recent deploys?

mike (runtime): There was a serving change ~45m ago that altered batching alignment and cache key normalization. I saw an uptick in average tokens-per-request on GPUs and a collapse in prefix cache hit rate.

sara (sre): show pool/instance status.

jenn (oncall): pool state: Desired=40, Running=30, PendingCreates=0, PendingScaleErrors=24. Autoscaler logs show provider-retry: "rate limit exceeded" and occasional "insufficient capacity".

leo (infra): provider side: rate limit on instance create, but also spot shortage in zone. We have a warm pool but it was configured for a different instance SKU and not compatible with current instance type.

devops: I can reconfigure warm pool to use a compatible SKU and attach +8 warm nodes immediately. Doing now.

mike (runtime): specifics of the regression: change 8d2b6ef updated prefix key hashing to include request metadata (trace_id) — which inadvertently made cache keys unique per request. Cache hit rate dropped from ~85% -> ~5%. Also batch alignment tweak disabled cross-request packing for small requests, raising per-request GPU time. Both together cut effective throughput per GPU by ~55%.

pauline (support): Customer-ops: multiple enterprise tenants reporting degraded throughput and timeouts. Creating incident bullet for status page.

alex (product): can we revert the key change quickly? If cache will warm back up then throughput should recover.

mike (runtime): preparing emergency revert. Command:

```
git revert 8d2b6ef --no-edit
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime --field-selector spec.template
```

Pushing in 2m. Also will re-enable cross-request packing flag.

incident-bot: Deploy started by mike (runtime). CI triggered. 

leo (infra): warm node attach done: +8 compatible GPUs assigned to pool. Running=38. This should buy us time while revert rolls out and caches warm.

jenn (oncall): routing mitigation: divert 20% of traffic for top throughput customers to us-west failover pool to reduce immediate pressure. Command applied:

```
rcli traffic adjust --from us-east-1 --to us-west-2 --pct 20 --policy gradual
```

Monitoring changes.

mike (runtime): revert complete, restart done. Watching prefix cache hit rate; added a short-lived metric to alert if cache-hit < 60% after deploy.

sara (sre): metrics: prefix cache hit recovered 7% -> 71% within 90s after revert. per-GPU effective requests/s back to within 10% of baseline. Queue trending down: 27k -> 8.6k in 8m.

devops: autoscaler still sees intermittent 429s but with warm nodes attached and traffic shift we're stable for now. Filed provider support case and requested quota increase.

pauline (support): posting customer update: "We've applied mitigations (rollback of recent serving change, extra warm capacity, partial regional routing). Performance is improving; some customers may still see delays as queues drain. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline for prevention."

alex (product): collecting impacted customer list and SLA owners. Can we quantify request-level impact?

mike (runtime): rough numbers: peak additional tail latency added ~1.8s median for affected requests. Error rate peaked ~0.9% for the region. Estimated total requests affected ~900k across the window. Top 10 tenants accounted for ~60% of the load during peak.

leo (infra): action items: 1) migrate warm pool SKUs to be multi-compatible; 2) add autoscaler backoff jitter for provider 429s; 3) ephemeral fallback to smaller-but-available instance SKUs when primary SKU unavailable. Raising CR: infra/auto-fallback-429.

sara (sre): runtime action items: 1) add pre-merge perf smoke for batching/cache metrics; 2) block deploys that reduce cache-hit by >10% vs baseline during canary; 3) add an alert for sudden cache-hit collapse (>30% drop in 5m).

jenn (oncall): handing off monitoring and PM to mike and sara. I'll remain reachable for 30m. Handoff: @mike (runtime) you take lead.

mike (runtime): taking handoff. Will coordinate postmortem with infra and devx. Proposed postmortem owner: mike (runtime).

incident-bot: Incident mitigated: mitigations applied (rollback + warm pool + traffic shift). Queue draining and metrics stabilizing. Next update scheduled in 1h or on change. :white_check_mark:

pauline (support): support queue still elevated but trending down. Will keep customers updated.

alex (product): scheduling postmortem tomorrow 11:00 EDT. Invite SRE, infra, runtime, devops, support.

mike (runtime): adding to postmortem notes: root cause = code-level change that injected non-deterministic cache keys + disabled packing; contributing factor = warm-pool SKU mismatch + provider quota/rate-limit. Remediations logged.

jenn (oncall): closing pager. Channel remains open for follow-ups. Nice work everyone. :clap:

incident-bot: Incident resolved: status=mitigated, resolution=rollback + warm-capacity + traffic-split. Postmortem owner=mike (runtime).
